summary: Feed s104_single is degraded: 1 of 6 checks failed. NDR port (10 Gbps) is overloaded by microbursts peaking at 14.46 Gbps (145% of capacity, 2 intervals). All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, one-way, drops) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering aggregated/bursty traffic without load-balancing or shaping. 1 ms microbursts peak at 14.46 Gbps, exceeding the 10 Gbps NDR ingress port/buffer (threshold 80% = 8 Gbps). This is classic oversubscription on a single tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR will tail-drop packets randomly during bursts, causing incomplete flows, missed detections, and reduced coverage despite needing full payload and both directions. Burst loss breaks NDR session reassembly and threat detection.

params.alternative: filter non-essential traffic if second port unavailable

recommended_fix.why: Distribute 14.46 Gbps bursts across 2x10 Gbps NDR ports (or a load-balanced tool group) with 5-tuple hashing to keep flows intact and preserve full payload required by NDR, preventing buffer overrun without slicing or filtering detection-relevant traffic.
